mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 5.0% over the past 3 months signals a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5.0% in the last 3 months
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 5.0%, SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a robust labor market that strengthens consumer confidence and corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction of PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of supply chain disruption (indicated by INDPRO below 95.0), manufacturing output contraction reduces corporate profit margins and increases input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO is below 95.0, SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the supply shock regime is below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST above 1,400,000 units) reflects strong consumer demand for housing and related sectors, which boosts economic activity and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST above 1,400,000 units fails to produce positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over 2-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate above 3.0% signals persistent inflationary pressure that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 260.0, SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the inflation threshold is below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-recovery phase of an economic cycle (indicated by PAYEMS growth above 100,000 jobs per month), the labor market expansion supports sustained consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the post-recovery labor market expansion regime, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over 2-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in manufacturing output (INDPRO below 95.0) and a downward revision to GDP growth (GDPC1 revision below 0.5% year-over-year) indicates a deepening supply shock that reduces corporate profitability and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction of INDPRO below 95.0 and GDPC1 downward revision fails to produce negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.
